blurb: The Signed System Volume (SSV) on macOS seals the entire operating system volume with a SHA-256-based Merkle hash tree, rooting the tree in a hash embedded in the signed boot manifest. Every file read from the system volume is verified against this tree by the kernel at the time of access; any tampered or corrupted file causes an immediate read error. The SSV mount is read-only and separate from the data volume, ensuring system files can never be modified at runtime. This architecture, combined with secure boot, provides end-to-end OS integrity from installation through every subsequent use.
